narrative_purpose: Makes the slowest clock in the chapter visible: over one Na'vi lifetime, Alpha Centauri B changes the character of Pandora's nights from orange-shadowed brightness to deep darkness.
subject: A split view of the exact same Pandoran forest clearing and the exact same ancient forked tree seen many decades apart. In the left half, one intense orange-white star burns high in the night and casts long crisp amber-edged shadows from the tree, while the bioluminescent plants remain visible. In the right half, the companion star is absent from the night hemisphere; the same tree and rocks are lit only by cyan-teal bioluminescence under a much darker star field. Polyphemus hangs in the same fixed position in both halves.
scene: Two moments in the eighty-year binary cycle, identical geography and viewing direction, separated only by the companion star's position and resulting night brightness.
camera: Locked wide eye-level landscape repeated side by side, like two naturalist observations from the same tripod position.
light: Left: strong directional orange-white starlight plus cool living underglow. Right: cool bioluminescent underglow only, with deep ambient shadow.
palette: Global cool night palette across both halves; restrained amber starlight and cast-shadow rims confined to the left half.
style: Painterly longitudinal field-observation plate, atmospheric and naturalistic rather than infographic-like.
detail_level: High detail on the repeated tree, rocks and shadows so the two halves clearly depict the same place; backgrounds soften into haze.
composition: Two equal halves with matching horizon and fixed planet position; left visibly bright and shadow-casting, right dark and bioluminescent.
consistency_notes: Both halves must be the same clearing and same Polyphemus. The only causal change is the brilliant companion star and its directional orange shadows on the left.
negative_prompt: no text, no labels, no seasonal foliage change, no day-night split, no different camera angles, no lens flare, no photographic or 3D-render look
